(0.9 bpg) | bbr = magloja01 }} '''Jamaal Dane Magloire''' (pronounced {{IPAc-en|j|ə|'|m|ɑː|l|_|m|ə|'|g|l|ɔːr}};{{cite AV media |title=1 March 2025 post |url=https://www.instagram.com/reel/DGpFnRlsjI5/ |date=1 March 2025 |time=00:02 |first=Jamaal |last=Magloire |publisher=Instagram}} born May 21, 1978) is a Canadian former professional [[basketball]] player who currently serves as basketball development consultant and community ambassador for the [[Toronto Raptors]].http://www.nba.com/raptors/mlsel_management.html. {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161104002243/http://www.nba.com/raptors/mlsel_management.html |date=November 4, 2016 }} He played 12 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for the [[Charlotte Hornets]], [[New Orleans Pelicans|New Orleans Hornets]], [[Milwaukee Bucks]], [[Portland Trail Blazers]], [[New Jersey Nets]], [[Dallas Mavericks]], [[Miami Heat]], and [[Toronto Raptors]]. The {{height|ft=6|in=11}}, {{convert|265|lb|kg st|abbr=on}} [[Center (basketball)|center]] was selected out of the [[University of Kentucky]] by the [[Charlotte Hornets]], with the 19th overall pick in the [[2000 NBA draft]], after withdrawing his name from the [[1999 NBA draft|previous draft]]. He was voted into the [[NBA All-Star Game]] in 2004, becoming the second Canadian All-Star in NBA history. In June 2026, ''[[Complex Networks|Complex]] Canada'' placed Magloire ninth in their ranking of ''The 20 Best Canadian Basketball Players of All Time''.{{Cite web |last=Wavvy |first=Mr. |date=2026-06-04 |title=The 20 Best Canadian Basketball Players of All Time, Ranked |url=https://www.complex.com/sports/a/mr-wavvy/best-canadian-basketball-players-all-time-ranked |access-date=2026-08-14| website=Complex |language=en}} ==Early life== Magloire was born in [[Toronto]], [[Ontario]], to [[Trinidad and Tobago|Trinidadian]] immigrant parents, Garth, a welder, and Marion, an insurance worker.{{Cite web |url=http://www.portlandtribune.com/sports/story.php?story_id=115524703111613800 |title=Portland Tribune |access-date=June 22, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110608035407/http://www.portlandtribune.com/sports/story.php?story_id=115524703111613800 |archive-date=June 8, 2011 |url-status=dead }}[https://www.thestar.com/sports/basketball/2011/12/16/finally_magloire_comes_home.html Finally, Magloire comes home] ''[[Toronto Star]]''. Accessed on January 2, 2016. He was raised in the city's [[Scarborough, Toronto|Scarborough]] district and attended high school at [[Eastern Commerce Collegiate Institute]], where he led the school's grade 12 boys basketball team to back-to-back Ontario provincial championships in 1995 and 1996.[http://www.ofsaa.on.ca/sites/default/files/Basketball%20-%20Boys'%20%20Past%20Champions.pdf OFSAA Past Champions Boys' Basketball] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304133318/http://www.ofsaa.on.ca/sites/default/files/Basketball%20-%20Boys'%20%20Past%20Champions.pdf |date=March 4, 2016 }} [[Ontario Federation of School Athletic Associations|OFSAA]]. Accessed on December 26, 2021. ==College career== In 1996, Magloire enrolled at the [[University of Kentucky]]. He was named to the SEC All-Freshman team in 1997.{{cite web |title=Kentucky 2017–18 Men's Basketball Media Guide |url=https://s3.amazonaws.com/ukathletics.com/documents/2017/10/19/1718_KentuckyMBB_MediaGuide_Web_1_.pdf |website=University of Kentucky |access-date=July 6, 2020}} Magloire started 12 games as a sophomore for the [[1997–98 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky Wildcats team]] that won the [[1998 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|national championship]] in 1998. He was a first-team All-[[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) selection in his senior season. He finished his college career as Kentucky's all-time leader in blocked shots, with 268. Magloire's tenure with the Wildcats earned him the nickname "Big Cat".{{cite news |last=Winderman |first=Ira |date=July 19, 2010 |title= Jamaal Magloire re-signs with Miami Heat to provide depth in the middle|url=https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/nba/2010/07/19/jamaal-magloire-re-signs-with/7597838007/ |work=[[The Palm Beach Post]] |location= |archive-date=July 22, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100722035708/http://www.palmbeachpost.com/sports/heat/jamaal-magloire-re-signs-with-miami-heat-to-810728.html |access-date=March 18, 2024}} ==NBA career== ===Charlotte / New Orleans Hornets (2000–2005)=== He was drafted by the [[Charlotte Hornets (1988–2002)|Charlotte Hornets]] with the 19th pick of the [[2000 NBA draft]], and filled a reserve role for his first two seasons in which he averaged 6.5 points in 16.8 minutes per game. In the [[2002–03 NBA season|2002–03 season]], the Hornets' first year in [[New Orleans]], he started all 82 games, averaging 10.3 points and 8.8 rebounds per game. During the [[2003–04 NBA season|2003–04]] season, Magloire averaged 13.6 points and 10.3 rebounds per game while starting all 82 games, and was named to the [[Eastern Conference (NBA)|Eastern Conference]] [[2004 NBA All-Star Game|All-Star Team]]. He became only the second Canadian All-Star in NBA history, after [[Steve Nash]]. Magloire played well, leading the Eastern All-Stars with 19 points,{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/allstar2004/allstar_game/ |title=NBA.com: NBA All-Star Game |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=March 16, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120115074125/http://www.nba.com/allstar2004/allstar_game/ |archive-date=January 15, 2012 |url-status=dead }} along with 8 rebounds in 21 minutes of action. ===Milwaukee Bucks (2005–2006)=== [[Image:Magloire 2.jpg|thumb|Magloire with the Milwaukee Bucks in 2006]] On October 26, 2005, he was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in exchange for [[Desmond Mason]], a [[Cedric Simmons|2006 first-round draft pick]] and cash considerations.{{cite web |title=Bucks Acquire Magloire In Trade With Hornets |url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/news/Magloire_Trade_051026.html |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=October 26, 2005 |access-date=March 21, 2009}} On January 21, 2006, Magloire recorded a career-high 22 rebounds and scored 13 points, during a 101–91 win over the [[Charlotte Bobcats]].[https://web.archive.org/web/20221216020411/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/260121015 Redd, Magloire pace Bucks in win over Bobcats] ===Portland Trail Blazers (2006–2007)=== On July 31, 2006, during the off-season, Magloire was traded to the Portland Trail Blazers for [[Steve Blake]], [[Ha Seung-Jin]], and [[Brian Skinner]].{{cite web |title=Trail Blazers Acquire All-Star Center Jamaal Magloire |url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/Jamaal_Magliore-185803-1218.html |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=July 31, 2006 |access-date=March 21, 2009}} Although Magloire has averaged nearly 10 points per game throughout his entire NBA career, he did not score over nine points in a single game during his first 20 games as a Trail Blazer. In fact, only eight times did Magloire record over 11 points during 81 regular season games in the [[2006–07 NBA season|2006–07 season]].[https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/498/jamaal-magloire ESPN - Jamaal Magloire Stats, News, Photos - New Jersey Nets - NBA Basketball] Magloire finished the season with an average of only 21 minutes played per game, down from 30 minutes played in the previous two seasons. Magloire became a free agent in the off-season. ===New Jersey Nets (2007–2008)=== The [[New Jersey Nets]] signed Magloire on July 17, 2007.{{cite web |title=NETS SIGN JAMAAL MAGLOIRE |url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/NETS_SIGN_JAMAAL_MAGLOIRE.html |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=July 17, 2007 |access-date=March 21, 2009}} In the [[2007–08 NBA season|2007–08 season]], he played little, averaging only 1.8 points and 3.4 rebounds per game. Magloire was waived by the Nets on February 22, 2008.{{cite web |title=NETS WAIVE JAMAAL MAGLOIRE |url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/Jamaal_Magloire_2_22_08.html |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=February 22, 2008 |access-date=March 21, 2009}} ===Dallas Mavericks (2008)=== The [[Dallas Mavericks]] signed Magloire on February 26, 2008, to back up centre [[Erick Dampier]] after former Maverick center [[DeSagana Diop]] was traded to the [[New Jersey Nets]] in the blockbuster trade involving point guards [[Devin Harris]] and [[Jason Kidd]].{{cite web |title=Mavs Sign Jamaal Magliore |url=http://www.nba.com/mavericks/news/mavs_sign_jamaal_magliore022608.html |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=February 26, 2008 |access-date=March 21, 2009}} ===Miami Heat (2008–2011)=== Magloire signed with the [[Miami Heat]] on August 30, 2008, for the veteran's minimum after nearing the luxury tax threshold.Ira Winderman, [http://blogs.sun-sentinel.com/sports_basketball_heat/2008/08/so-what-does-71.html So what does $71.2 million get you?] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080902002521/http://blogs.sun-sentinel.com/sports_basketball_heat/2008/08/so-what-does-71.html |date=September 2, 2008 }}, August 29, 2009 Magloire provided additional depth and experience at the centre position. He was upgraded to starter on Monday, January 26, 2009, vs. the Atlanta Hawks.{{Cite web |url=http://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/basketball/heat/sfl-flspheat30newsbaug30,0,1250216.story |title=Magloire shores up depth |access-date=August 30, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080902002603/http://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/basketball/heat/sfl-flspheat30newsbaug30,0,1250216.story |archive-date=September 2, 2008 |url-status=dead }} Miami re-signed Magloire with the Heat for the [[2009–10 NBA season|2009–10 season]]. Magloire was valued as an enforcer during his tenure with Miami. On July 19, 2010, the Heat re-signed Magloire for the [[2010–11 NBA season|2010–11 season]].{{cite news |title=Canadian Magloire re-signs with Miami Heat |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/canadian-magloire-re-signs-with-miami-heat-1.966015 |work=[[CBC.ca]] |date=July 19, 2010 |access-date=July 22, 2010}} The Heat would make it to the [[2011 NBA Finals]], and fell short to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in six games."[http://www.nba.com/2010/news/07/19/heat.magloire.ap/index.html?ls=iref:nbahpt2 Heat continue to fill roster, re-sign Magloire]". Associated Press. July 19, 2010. ===Toronto Raptors (2011–2012)=== On December 9, 2011, Magloire signed a one-year deal with his hometown team the [[Toronto Raptors]] for the veteran's minimum. This marked the first time a Canadian born player played for the Raptors, the only NBA franchise in Canada."[http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/20111209/21881/raptors-sign-veteran-centre-jamaal-magloire Raptors sign veteran centre Jamaal Magloire]". NBA. December 9, 2011. Magloire re-signed with the team on September 18, 2012,{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=10941 |title=Toronto Raptors sign center Jamaal Magloire |date=September 18, 2012 |access-date=February 26, 2021}} but was waived by the team on October 27, 2012.{{cite news| url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/nba/raptors-waive-canadian-centre-jamaal-magloire-1.1176478 | title= Raptors waive Canadian centre Jamaal Magloire | work=CBC News}} After being waived by the Raptors, Magloire would not play again in the NBA. Thus, his final NBA game was played on April 26, 2012, in a 98–67 win over the New Jersey Nets (the lowest amount of points the Nets scored that season). In his final game, Magloire was the Raptors' starting Center, he played for 5 minutes and recorded 4 rebounds. ==NBA career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend|leader=y}} ===Regular season=== || 18 || 19.8 || .470 || .000 || .682 || 5.3 || .5 || .2 || .9 || 7.3 {{s-end}} ==Post-playing career== On November 18, 2012, the Toronto Raptors hired Magloire as their basketball development consultant and community ambassador. The role involves Magloire assisting the Raptors' coaching staff with the individual skill development of their players in practices and games, while also making corporate/community appearances throughout the season on behalf of the team.{{Cite web |url=https://www.cbc.ca/shootthemessenger/cast/jamaal-magloire |title=Shoot the Messenger Cast: Jamaal Magloire | work=CBC.ca | access-date=February 26, 2021}}{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11472 |title=Toronto Raptors hire Jamaal Magloire as development consultant and community ambassador |work=InsideHoops.com |date=November 18, 2012 |access-date=February 26, 2021}} ==Personal life== In the early morning hours of June 23, 2001, Magloire's half-brother, 19-year-old Justin Sheppard, was shot and killed on the footbridge that spans [[Castle Frank Brook|the ravine around Rosedale Valley Road]] between [[Bloor Street]] East and Glen Road near [[Sherbourne (TTC)|Sherbourne subway station]] in Toronto. Like Magloire, Sheppard was a promising basketball talent at Eastern Commerce, and was supposed to begin a scholarship at a [[Maryland]] prep school that fall. Magloire helped post a [[Canadian dollar|CAD $]]50,000 reward, but to date, there have been no arrests and the killing remains unsolved.[http://www.netsdaily.com/blog/?p=363 NetsDaily Blog » Archive »
